verdict: Mostly confirmed: every table entry and nearly every number reproduces, and 94 independent refits match the result files bit for bit; 24 corrected claims, 2 unsupported statements, 10 omissions. All 60 cells of the section-1 table, all family and per-seed numbers, the paired and unpaired nulls (33 null cells re-run: identical), the P2 parity predictions, the block-power re-thresholding, the nosmalln/nobg identities with the atlas counterfactuals (126/126, 224/231, and the CV switch in all 7 unequal cells), the labelnoise effects, the core against DFG alone, against nets_best (recomputed from the network files) and against the paired null, the compute, and every leave-one-in n* reproduce with my own code. 94 refits with my own instrumented copy of the frozen file (all 38 cells of refits.json and 56 more) equal the result files bit for bit and confirm nearly every model description. Corrections: (1) training sets do not come from the fit rng; (2) 38 refits, not 36; (3) nosums denominators (31 and 9 higher include the 3 lost targets); (4) nosmalln is on compositions and formulas, not mixtures; (5) the unpaired null overstates the like-for-like paired null 20-30-fold, not about tenfold; (6) the P2 rule uses a 0.45 floor, not 'DFG alone's own error'; (7) delta can change the n = 16 variant choice; (8) lenient-higher targets are first fitted at 32-256, not 32-64; (9) majpar at delta = 0.9: chi[x3,x4] passes in round 1 but the n/2 room is full; (10) strict lowers one formula (f7_02), not two; (11) f7_10 reaches 10% through a modulated block at its n_detect, not through characters before it; (12) the 10%-point sentence fails for 5 of the 23; (13) K enters the character and sum-block tests, not the linear or spectral ones; (14) par4 under K3 is also missed at 64 and 128, where it would pass; (15) attribution 'local / extension' is a largest-score convention: the global test also admits those characters; (16) rand1 has 5 relevant inputs (3 with degree-1 weight); (17) labelnoise: the block test's effective threshold rises 1/s^2 = 1.98x for far9, not 1.4x; (18) the nets_best comparison is over 126 targets; (19) the 12 gains are 8 formulas, and3 and 3 mixtures, h5rf0 at 164; plus wording points (what moved under nosums, the paired-null rationale, the f7_01 linear block's 29, the par4-as-evidence heuristic, fd_11 61 -> 62, the post-hoc list). Unsupported: the '(paper, Table 1)' citation for h6_10, and 'loses exactly where a removed part has no substitute' (13 of the 26 losses restored, 2 in part, h5s2 unexplained, 10 untested).

omissions: f7_10 = [x1+...+x5 + 2 x6 <= -1] is a halfspace (a weighted threshold with one boundary) by families.py's own stated rule, but it is classed as a mixture, following ATLAS.md section 1.9. As a halfspace it would change, for example, strict's halfspace mean from -0.23 to -0.17 (4/2 over 8).

The refits' 'class that admitted it' is the class whose test gave the largest score (calib_rec.feat_chi), not the first or only class to pass. In the cited cells characters attributed to the local class or an extension also pass the same round's global test: chi[x1,x2,x3] and chi[x3,x4] in both mux n = 256 refits, and chi[x5] in rand3 n = 128. That matters for the reading that 'the composition classes reach' degree-4 targets' lower-degree structure.

K3 par4: the block is missed at n = 64 and 128 too, where it would pass. The search finds it in 3 of the 9 grid points from n = 64, which is a sharper statement of the 'luck' than the four cells listed.

h6_10: DFG alone's weighted block at n = 256 is |s + 3 x13|, while the target is [|s - 3 x13| > 1]: the relative sign is wrong. The best function of |s + 3 x13| has error 0.0195 (exact, over uniform inputs), so the 0.017 is that block's irreducible error, as Part 10's paper noted for v3's member. The leave-one-in conclusion is unaffected.
'Share' is used two ways: absolute sd of a term's contribution (mux 0.51, par4 0.61) and fraction of the model's sd (h6_10 0.96, absolute 0.85).

No significance or uncertainty is given for the 'removable' and 'carry' readings beyond counts against the null. The null has 1 (one seed) or 3 (two seeds) moved targets, so lsread's and K3's 3 moves on one seed cannot be told from it. The core's 54 against the null's 8, and nosums, are clear.

Ten of the core's 26 clearly-higher targets (h5rf1, h6_03, rf01, mux11, rf19, h6_07, rmaj9, thrsum, fd_00, rand3) were not examined by the leave-one-in runs, and h5s2 is not restored by any part tried. Neither is said in section 6, and they bear on the 'loses exactly where' claim.

The majpar delta = 0.9 refit shows a second way the linear block costs data at small n, not mentioned: its 30 characters use up the n/2 least-squares room (p <= n/2), so a character that passes in the next round cannot enter.
The short answer labels interpretive statements (e.g. 'Four parts are removable') as Numerical; the numbers are numerical, the reading is Heuristic.
